**Who’s considered the “father of the computer?”**  
The title most often goes to **Charles Babbage** (1791‑1871). In the 1830s he designed the **Analytical Engine**, a mechanical device that had many of the core concepts of today’s computers—programmable instructions, a central processing unit, and memory. Though it was never built in his lifetime, Babbage’s ideas laid the groundwork for modern computing, earning him that honorary nickname.
